 Posco, CATL signs 3-year lithium supply deal
 Published : Nov. 18, 2026 - 17:46:27
 Updated : Nov. 18, 2026 - 17:53:44 
 Add The Korea Herald on Google
 Link copied!
 Byun Hye-jin 
 Subscribe + 
 Posco Group’s brine lithium production facility in Argentina (Posco Group) Posco Group said Wednesday it finalized a three-year lithium supply deal with CATL, the world’s largest electric vehicle battery manufacturer, expanding its footprint in a global critical minerals market long dominated by China.
 Running 2026-2028, the agreement aims to forge a long-term partnership and establish a stable raw materials supply chain.
 Details of the contract, including where the lithium will be sourced and its target market, remain undisclosed due to confidentiality. Posco operates a brine lithium facility in Argentina, while holding an equity stake and concentrate supply rights in Australia.
 Notably, Posco Holdings completed the upstream facility for its second brine lithium plant in Argentina last month, lifting total annual capacity — including its first plant — to 48,000 tons.
 Under Posco Group Chairman Chang In-hwa’s “Triple Core” strategy, the group aims to establish an annual lithium production capacity of 173,000 tons by 2033 and generate more than 1.8 trillion won ($1.35 billion) in operating profit from its lithium business by 2035.
 Building on its materials procurement and development capabilities in steelmaking, Posco Group has been diversifying its portfolio by leveraging high-grade lithium resources.
 The company said the deal strengthens its lithium sales base in China by landing CATL, which accounts for roughly 40 percent of the global EV battery market.
 The move also aligns with Chang’s push to secure high-quality resources and expand partnerships with major global clients.
 Posco Group plans to contribute to South Korea’s resilience in strategic resources and help stabilize global critical mineral supply chains, while boosting its production capacity, sales competitiveness and profitability.
